tasks.short: Commission and assess research on strategic or operational issues.

steps.what: Define the research question, decision deadline and evidence needed.
Gather internal evidence and external research database results.
Read sources and distinguish supported findings, conflicting evidence and gaps.

loop.input: Approved research evidence, source register and research brief.
loop.output: Evidence table with quoted passages, source locations, contradictions and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Verify source locations and quotations mechanically; the analyst checks relevance, credibility and consequential claims.
loop.stop: One extraction pass and one correction per source within the agreed corpus; unreadable or unsupported items return to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Sources express comparable claims in different prose, formats and terminology.

steps.what: Interview operating leaders and specialists about gaps and practical constraints.
Compare options and write findings, limitations and recommendations.

loop.input: Reviewed evidence table, expert notes and deterministic option calculations.
loop.output: Research paper separating evidence, assumptions, options and limitations.
loop.check: Check figures against calculations and citations against the evidence table; the analyst reviews reasoning and omissions.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision within the approved brief; unresolved contradictions remain explicit.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template can assemble figures, but synthesising prose and explaining conflicting evidence requires language interpretation.

steps.what: Challenge the findings and test their implications with operating leaders.
Choose a recommendation or commission further investigation within delegated authority.
Record agreed actions, owners and review dates.

tasks.design: A research workspace in the {DOCS} takes a structured brief and imports approved evidence through the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Bounded extraction and drafting loops produce a cited evidence table and research paper, with deterministic figure checks and analyst approval. The chief executive makes the decision, then configured rules create agreed actions in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Research questions change, sources use inconsistent formats, and trustworthy synthesis needs judgement. Gathering evidence across repositories also required repeated manual work.
tasks.enabler_now: Standard connectors, document parsers and bounded language models can assemble and explain an approved corpus. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort needed to build the retrieval and checking glue.
tasks.still_hard: Source quality, missing evidence, causal inference and commercially sensitive assumptions still need experienced scrutiny. Licensed research and restricted internal data may be expensive to connect.
tasks.human_edge: Choose questions worth answering, recognise misleading certainty, challenge interested parties and decide what evidence justifies action.

ambition.what: Monthly review of customer demand assumptions before committing operating capacity.

tasks.altitude: The chief executive spends less preparation time locating and reconciling evidence, and more time challenging assumptions with operating leaders. Existing delegated decision rights remain; faster evidence supports earlier recommendations to the board.

reach.task: Turn a research recommendation into a measured operational pilot.
reach.learn: Define a baseline, comparison group, stopping rule and operational success measure.

evidence.claim: Board Intelligence Report Writer drafts structured papers from management documents; this supports the drafting component, not independent research validity.
Copilot in Power BI supports report summaries and data questions; the digest warns that unprepared data models produce inaccurate answers.
Deterministic retrieval, source checks and bounded drafting are a plausible design; the effort and remaining-time estimates are not measured outcomes.
The digest documents a report containing nonexistent references and a fabricated court case, supporting explicit citation verification.

assumptions: This is a project-based research task with analyst support, rather than continuous academic research.
Time shares estimate combined active human effort across the workflow, not elapsed project time or only chief executive time.
Initial scope covers approved repositories and supplied external research, with file imports available before full integration.
Access estimates include active permission and consultation work where national rules apply; elapsed approval time may be longer.
Personal data handling must satisfy GDPR; employee consultation depends on the use and national rules.
unknowns: Which research topics recur often enough to justify reusable source collections?
Which repositories and external research licences permit automated retrieval and processing?
Who supplies analyst support and approves evidence quality?
Which decisions are delegated to the chief executive and which are reserved for the board?
Does the proposed use require employee consultation under applicable national rules?
research_questions: Can analysts trace every consequential claim in a pilot paper to an accessible source?
Does the bounded synthesis retain contrary evidence and uncertainty?
How much active time is spent gathering evidence versus interpreting it?
new_work: Review extracted claims, source credibility and omitted counterarguments.
Resolve inaccessible sources and inconsistent management figures.
Maintain source permissions, connectors and document templates.
Update the research corpus and retire stale findings.

tasks.short: Oversee site, construction and equipment programmes from business need to acceptance.

steps.what: Set programme outcomes, constraints and executive sponsorship.
Collect proposals, site information, technical requirements and approval conditions.

loop.input: Supplier proposals, site information and technical requirements.
loop.output: Option register with quoted prices, exclusions, dates, dependencies and source locations.
loop.check: Validate currencies, units and required fields; facilities and procurement specialists verify consequential terms against originals.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction per document; missing or ambiguous terms become exceptions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Proposals contain inconsistent prose and exclusions that fixed field mappings cannot reliably capture.

steps.what: Inspect shortlisted sites or equipment with technical specialists.
Compare lifecycle costs, funding requirements and delivery scenarios.
Negotiate major trade-offs, responsibilities and delivery commitments with counterparties.
Approve programme funding and conditions within delegated authority.
Issue purchase orders against approved funding and agreed terms.
Reconcile milestone updates, spend and risks into a programme status report.
Resolve material delays, scope changes and funding exceptions.
Inspect completed work and confirm acceptance against technical requirements.

tasks.design: A programme register in the {PROJECT} links proposal evidence in the {DOCS}, approved orders in the {PROCUREMENT} and actual spend in the {ERP}. A bounded extraction loop prepares comparable proposal fields; deterministic calculations produce lifecycle appraisals and milestone dashboards in the {BI}. Investment approval, negotiations, material changes and technical acceptance stay with authorised people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Proposal terms, project updates and finance records sit in separate places. Projects are infrequent, so bespoke integration often cost more than the expected administrative saving.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing project and purchasing workflows can hold approvals and milestones. Faster custom integration and bounded proposal extraction make a small reusable programme register more economical.
tasks.still_hard: Physical conditions, planning constraints, construction risk, negotiation and technical acceptance remain specialist work. Forecasts cannot remove supplier uncertainty or guarantee delivery.
tasks.human_edge: Balance long-term capacity, capital exposure, workforce needs and counterparties' incentives while accepting responsibility for irreversible commitments.

ambition.what: Weekly review of capital cash-flow exposure and critical milestone delays during active programmes.

tasks.altitude: During active programmes, the chief executive receives a short exception view and spends more time resolving trade-offs with the general and operations manager. Faster visibility supports earlier intervention within existing capital authority.

reach.task: Plan operational readiness for a new site or major equipment installation.
reach.learn: Map commissioning dependencies, staffing readiness, disruption costs and acceptance criteria.

evidence.claim: A programme register, deterministic capital appraisal and configured purchasing approvals are established software patterns.
Copilot in Power BI supports report summaries and data questions; this supports reporting preparation rather than construction control.
Pigment describes anomaly detection and planning reports; this supports financial monitoring components rather than site selection or technical acceptance.
The proposed time savings and implementation ranges are estimates, with no matching end-to-end case in the digest.

assumptions: This describes executive oversight; specialists manage construction and perform technical inspections.
Time shares estimate combined active human effort for a representative programme, not construction duration or only chief executive time.
The programme fits delegated capital authority; board-reserved commitments require the corresponding board decision before release.
Calculations use explicit assumptions and comparable units; qualitative site suitability is not automatically scored.
Access estimates include active consultation work where workplace changes trigger national rules; statutory waiting periods and external permits are excluded.
unknowns: Is the programme a site move, construction project, equipment purchase or routine supply programme?
Which funding, contracting and change decisions require board approval?
Are purchase orders, milestones and capital spend consistently coded?
Which technical, legal and planning specialists must approve the project?
Which workplace changes require consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Can one completed programme be reconciled from approval through orders, spend and acceptance?
Which proposal exclusions materially changed the eventual lifecycle cost?
Would structured milestone updates remove enough consolidation work to justify integration?
new_work: Verify extracted prices, exclusions, dependencies and approval conditions.
Maintain lifecycle cost assumptions and milestone definitions.
Investigate unmatched orders, stale updates and forecast exceptions.
Maintain delegated approval limits and access permissions.
Check that completed work meets specialist acceptance criteria.

tasks.short: Represent the organisation at official functions or appoint a suitable representative.

steps.what: Log the invitation, purpose, audience and response deadline.
Choose attendance, delegation or decline and define the representative's mandate.
Gather approved positions, audience information and relevant relationship history.
Draft talking points, likely questions and boundaries on commitments.

loop.input: Approved positions, event brief, permitted relationship context and representative mandate.
loop.output: Talking points, possible questions and explicit limits on commitments.
loop.check: Trace factual claims to approved evidence; communications staff check tone, audience fit and mandate consistency.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported claims are removed or returned for clarification.
loop.why_not_simpler: Adapting approved positions to a particular audience and occasion requires contextual writing.

steps.what: Approve messages and clarify sensitive positions with the representative.
Confirm the representative and arrange attendance details with the organiser.
Attend, speak, listen and build relationships within the agreed mandate.
Record commitments and draft follow-up messages from the representative's notes.

loop.input: Representative-supplied event notes and explicit external commitments.
loop.output: Draft actions and follow-up messages distinguishing promises from suggestions.
loop.check: Link actions to notes; the representative verifies recipients, commitments, owners and dates.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; ambiguous promises remain questions and are never sent automatically.
loop.why_not_simpler: Informal notes need contextual interpretation to distinguish discussion from an actual commitment.

steps.what: Approve and send follow-up messages, then assign agreed actions.

tasks.design: A configured event register links invitations in the {EMAIL}, availability in the {CALENDAR} and approved positions in the {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop prepares sourced talking points and follow-up drafts, while the representative approves messages and commitments. Configured flows send approved confirmations and follow-ups, and record agreed actions in the {PROJECT} and relevant relationship history in the {CRM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Invitations, approved messages and relationship context were scattered, while attendance and representation depended heavily on personal judgement. Occasional events rarely justified a custom workflow.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured forms, calendar links and reusable templates handle coordination. Bounded drafting can adapt approved material and prepare follow-up without automating the live relationship.
tasks.still_hard: Reading the room, handling unexpected questions and protecting trust remain human work. Sensitive commitments and public wording require careful review.
tasks.human_edge: Bring credibility, listen for unstated concerns, judge the moment and make accountable commitments in person.

ambition.what: Regional operations managers represent the organisation at local industry forums with an approved briefing and mandate.

tasks.altitude: The chief executive spends less time assembling briefs and coordinating attendance, and can delegate suitable events with clearer limits. Delegates gain explicit authority to speak within the agreed mandate.

reach.task: Represent operational priorities at a local industry or community forum.
reach.learn: Handle challenging questions, distinguish discussion from commitment and escalate matters outside the mandate.

evidence.claim: Configured invitation tracking, calendar coordination and approved message dispatch are established workflow patterns.
Board Intelligence Report Writer demonstrates drafting structured material from management documents; event briefing is an adjacent proposed use.
The cross-government trial reported drafting savings with human oversight; its findings do not establish savings for executive representation.
The digest identifies editorial responsibility and human review as relevant to AI-assisted public-interest text under AI Act Article 50.

assumptions: The event involves live representation; formal travel booking and expense reimbursement are separate tasks.
Time shares estimate combined active human effort, with live attendance dominating; they exclude travel time.
Invitation fields are entered or confirmed through a structured form; free-text invitation parsing is outside the first build.
Follow-up drafting uses supplied notes, without requiring event recording.
GDPR applies to relationship data, and AI Act transparency duties must be assessed for applicable public communications.
Access estimates cover active permission work and any applicable consultation under national rules; elapsed approvals may take longer.
unknowns: Which event types may be delegated, and to whom?
Where are approved positions and sensitive-topic instructions maintained?
Which relationship records may briefing staff and delegates access?
Who can approve public statements and external commitments?
Which public communications trigger specific disclosure or review requirements?
research_questions: Can a delegate use the briefing to answer likely questions without exceeding the mandate?
Do drafted follow-ups distinguish commitments from conversational suggestions?
How much preparation can be reused across recurring event types?
new_work: Maintain approved positions, evidence dates and delegation mandates.
Review talking points for factual accuracy and audience fit.
Confirm commitments before sending follow-up messages.
Keep relationship records proportionate, accurate and access-controlled.
Handle unusual invitations and scheduling exceptions.

role.altitude: The chief executive's week contains less evidence assembly and coordination, with more time for strategic challenge, investment trade-offs and external relationships. Formal authority changes only through explicit board or executive delegation.
reach: Work with the general and operations manager to translate research into measured pilots.
Connect capital decisions to operational readiness and commissioning.
Delegate suitable external representation with clear speaking and commitment limits.
skills_to_grow: Frame research questions around decisions and evidence thresholds.
Challenge sources, causal claims and scenario assumptions.
Interpret lifecycle costs, capital exposure and delivery dependencies.
Set practical delegation mandates and coach representatives.
Review sourced drafts and manage exceptions without redoing all preparation.
role.ambitious_version: Run a shorter evidence-to-decision cycle: review demand assumptions monthly, intervene weekly on active capital risks, and develop operations managers as credible external representatives.
